text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 5.3% today after oil prices dropped sharply on news that Iran signaled willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. eases military pressure, raising hopes for a diplomatic settlement to U.S.-Iran tensions. Crude oil reversed earlier gains and tumbled below $100 a barrel on this optimism, which is a significant headwind for refiners — they profit most when oil prices are high and volatile, so a move toward lower, more stable prices reduces their margins.

The stock's decline extends a broader retreat after hitting a peak of $424.89 on September 18th. Refineries are running at very high utilization (96.8%), and storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain healthy, so the weakness is driven almost entirely by the shift in geopolitical risk and oil pricing rather than operational constraints.
